description: Make the generated Word report visually match the user's original Word file. Two visual targets from the user's screenshots: (A) the 'Cost Summary Differences' page - centered+underlined title; a single bordered (Table Grid) table whose No/Account Name/Account ID cells are VERTICALLY MERGED (w:vMerge) down the whole service list as one tall '1 | JUST UDO AVIATION PRIVATE LIMITED (Fly91)/ Greatworx | 674351849978' cell; a 'No' header rendered stacked 'N' over 'o'; bold two-line Last Week / Current Week headers with the date ranges on the second line; one service per row with centered cost cells; a final Total Cost row whose leading columns are MERGED (gridSpan) into one centered bold 'Total Cost' cell with cost columns reading '($728.33 Tax Excluded Cost)' / '($705.25 Tax Excluded Cost)'. (B) a professional COVER page as page 1: company logo in the top-right, a blue vertical accent bar down the left edge, the title, and (if a cover_background asset is configured) a full-page background image behind it. Match page size (US Letter 12240x15840 twips) and tighten margins toward the reference. All image choices come from a configurable assets mapping in config.json so the client can swap in their own Greatworx logo + real Fly91 screenshots without code changes. The DESIGN must be data-agnostic (identical for mock and real data). Keep Python 3.9 compatible and keep the Excel path and --format {docx,xlsx,both} working. This is a single coherent feature; implement all of it, then iterate (regenerate + re-verify) until the extended verifier passes.
steps: In report/word_report.py add a config-driven assets accessor: read config['word_report']['assets'] (a dict mapping logical names -> file paths) with defaults {logo: 'assets/logo.png', cover_background: 'assets/cover_background.png', inspector_critical/high/medium/low, guardduty, cost_overview -> the stable-named assets/ files}. Resolve paths relative to the repo root. Any asset that does not exist on disk must be skipped gracefully (never crash) so the report still generates when the client has not supplied an image.

Set page size and margins to match the reference section. Use the document's section (doc.sections[0]): set page_width/page_height to US Letter (python-docx: from docx.shared import Inches/Emu; width=Inches(8.5), height=Inches(11)), and tighten margins toward the reference section (reference first section twips: top=1340 right=0 bottom=1160 left=360 header=0 footer=970). Choose sane non-zero margins close to these (e.g. left ~0.25in, right small, top ~0.9in) while keeping tables within the printable area. Record exact chosen EMU/inches values in findings.

Rewrite _build_cover to produce a professional cover page as PAGE 1: (a) a thin full-height BLUE vertical accent bar on the LEFT edge - implement via a 1x1 bordered/shaded table column or an OxmlElement shading rectangle sized to page height, color a professional blue (e.g. 1F4E79 / 2E74B5); (b) the LOGO (assets/logo.png) placed TOP-RIGHT (use a right-aligned paragraph or a 1-row table with the logo in the right cell, add_picture with a reasonable width ~1.8in); (c) the report title (word_cfg['report_title']) large, the client_org, 'Submitted By <submitter_org>', and the reporting period, as in the current cover; (d) if assets['cover_background'] EXISTS on disk, place it as a full-page background behind the content (python-docx limitation: use an anchored/behind-text floating drawing sized to the full page via OOXML wp:anchor with behindDoc=1, or if impractical, add it sized to page width at the top and document the limitation). If cover_background is absent (the default - the reference set has NO cityscape), render the cover WITHOUT a background photo (logo + blue bar + title only) and do not fail. End the cover with a page break so Cost Summary starts on page 2.

In _build_cost_summary_differences: (1) Replace doc.add_heading('Cost Summary Differences', level=1) title with a CENTERED, UNDERLINED title - a paragraph centered (WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER) whose run has run.underline=True (and bold, sized like a heading). The verifier will look for an underlined centered run containing 'Cost Summary Differences'.

In the cost table header row: build the 'No' header cell so it renders STACKED as 'N' over 'o' (two lines: add run 'N', then a line break w:br, then run 'o' - or two paragraphs in the cell). Build 'Last Week' and 'Current Week' header cells as BOLD with the date range on a SECOND line: first line bold 'Last Week' then a line break then the previous-period range (e.g. '07th Sep - 13th Sep)'), and 'Current Week' then line break then '(14th Sep - 20th Sep)'. Derive the date-range strings from self._previous_range_str()/_current_range_str() so they track the actual reporting period (keep the literal screenshot format as close as the helpers allow; it is fine if the exact day-ordinal formatting differs slightly as long as the two-line bold structure and the period dates are present).

Vertically MERGE the No / Account Name / Account ID columns across all service rows: build the service rows first (one row per service, with the account identity values only needed in the first row), then merge table cell (first_service_row, col) down to (last_service_row, col) for col in (0,1,2) using cell_top.merge(cell_bottom) (python-docx) which emits w:vMerge. The merged col0 shows '1', col1 shows self._account_name(), col2 shows self._account_id(), vertically centered. Do NOT leave the per-row cells blank-after-first (the current behavior) - they must be a real vertical merge so the XML carries w:vMerge markers.
Center the Last Week / Current Week cost cells (WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER) in every service row.

Total Cost row: merge the leading cells (No, Account Name, Account ID, Services -> indices 0..3) into ONE cell (cell0.merge(cell1).merge(...) which emits w:gridSpan or merged tc), set its text to 'Total Cost' centered and bold; set the two cost columns to the '(<total> Tax Excluded Cost)' labels - KEEP the existing total label logic (cost.get('total_*_label') or '<currency> Tax Excluded Cost') but ensure the rendered text matches the screenshot style '($728.33 Tax Excluded Cost)' with surrounding parentheses when the label is auto-generated. Center+bold the cost cells.

Make the Inspector/GuardDuty embedded visuals use the configurable asset screenshots when present: in _embed_inspector_screenshots and _build_guardduty, prefer embedding the mapped asset image (assets['inspector_critical'/'high'/'medium'/'low'], assets['guardduty']) via doc.add_picture(path, width=Inches(6)) when that asset exists on disk; otherwise fall back to the existing report/screenshots.py runtime renderer. This keeps the demo looking like the original (real console captures) while remaining swappable. Preserve the existing captions and graceful-degradation behavior.

Set a sensible document default font/size to approximate the reference (e.g. doc.styles['Normal'].font.name and size ~10-11pt) so the body reads like the screenshots; the title larger. Keep it modest - do not break existing table styling.

Ensure every new raw-OOXML helper (vMerge, gridSpan merge, cell shading for the accent bar, floating background, line breaks, borders, pgSz/pgMar) is Python 3.9 compatible and wrapped so a failure degrades gracefully (log + continue) rather than aborting the whole document.

EXTEND scripts/verify_word_report.py with DESIGN assertions (unzip the .docx and parse word/document.xml with the stdlib zipfile + a lightweight XML/string scan, in addition to python-docx): (a) title run for 'Cost Summary Differences' is underlined AND its paragraph is centered; (b) word/document.xml contains w:vMerge markers (the account-identity vertical merge); (c) the Total Cost row has a merged leading cell (w:gridSpan or a merged tc) - assert the merge marker is present; (d) the header contains the two-line bold date-range text (e.g. 'Last Week' and 'Current Week' with the period dates present); (e) the cover page has an embedded image (logo) - word/media has at least the Inspector/GuardDuty images PLUS the cover logo (assert media image count >= 6, and assert the logo is referenced on page 1 / before the Cost Summary table); (f) pgSz is Letter (w:w=12240 w:h=15840) and pgMar is present and matches the chosen values. Keep ALL existing content checks. Add a '--design' flag or run these unconditionally; make sure the script still accepts the existing args (path, --contains, --min-images).

ITERATE: regenerate the docx (python3 weekly_bau_report.py --start-date 2026-09-14 --end-date 2026-09-20 --mock --format docx --output demo/Fly91_Weekly_Status_Report_14-20_Sep_2026.docx) then run the extended verifier with --min-images 7; if any design assertion FAILS, fix the code and regenerate; repeat until ALL CHECKS PASSED. Do not finish until the loop converges.

No-regression: run python3 weekly_bau_report.py ... --format both and python3 weekly_bau_report.py ... --format xlsx (or default) and confirm the Excel file still generates without error. Also run scripts/verify_word_live_fallback.py if it applies to confirm the live/non-mock-shaped path still builds the same design (feed real-shaped data to prove design is data-agnostic).

Prove design is data-agnostic: generate a docx from a NON-mock-looking dataset (e.g. different account values / costs, still via the same code path) and confirm the extended verifier's DESIGN assertions (merges, underline title, cover, pgSz) still pass - the structure must not depend on the mock flag. Document how you simulated this.

Update README.md: add a short section documenting (1) how to run on REAL AWS data in CloudShell (no --mock, --format docx/both), (2) that the embedded logo + screenshots are from the Operisoft/Aptech reference sample and should be replaced with the client's own Greatworx logo and real Fly91 captures by editing config.json word_report.assets paths (or dropping files at assets/logo.png etc.), (3) that the design (cover, table merges, fonts, page size) is identical for mock and real data, (4) the known python-docx full-bleed cover-background limitation and that assets/cover_background.png (a cityscape) is optional and not shipped. Add config.json word_report.assets with the default mapping.
Regenerate demo/Fly91_Weekly_Status_Report_14-20_Sep_2026.docx with the final design so the committed demo reflects it.
acceptance_criteria: The generated docx title 'Cost Summary Differences' is centered and underlined (verifier asserts underline + center)
word/document.xml contains w:vMerge markers for the No/Account Name/Account ID columns spanning the service rows (one tall account-identity cell showing '1', the account name, and 674351849978)
The Total Cost row's leading columns are merged into a single centered bold 'Total Cost' cell; cost columns read '(<total> Tax Excluded Cost)'
The cost table header has a stacked 'N'/'o' No column and bold two-line Last Week / Current Week headers carrying the period date ranges
Page 1 is a cover with the logo top-right, a blue left accent bar, and the title; word/media contains the cover logo image (media image count >= 6)
Page size is US Letter (pgSz w:w=12240 w:h=15840) and margins match the chosen reference-aligned values
config.json has a word_report.assets mapping and swapping those paths changes the embedded logo/screenshots with no code change; missing assets degrade gracefully
python3 scripts/verify_word_report.py <docx> --min-images 7 prints ALL CHECKS PASSED including the new design assertions
--format both and --format xlsx (default) still generate the Excel report without error (no regression)
Design assertions still pass when generated from a non-mock-looking dataset (data-agnostic)
Code is Python 3.9 compatible (no 'X | None' unions); demo/Fly91_Weekly_Status_Report_14-20_Sep_2026.docx regenerated
verification: python3 -c "import zipfile; d=zipfile.ZipFile('demo/Fly91_Weekly_Status_Report_14-20_Sep_2026.docx').read('word/document.xml').decode(); assert 'vMerge' in d; assert d.count('<w:pgSz')>0; print('vMerge', d.count('vMerge'))"
findings:
COMPLETED & GREEN. Commit cbeb594 on feat/word-report-design-match (not pushed). 12 files changed, 600 insertions, 35 deletions.

WHAT CHANGED (report/word_report.py):
- Added config-driven asset accessor: DEFAULT_ASSETS mapping + self.assets merged from config['word_report']['assets']; _asset_path(name) resolves relative paths against repo root (_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent) and returns None (skip gracefully) when the file is absent. Inspector (4 severities), GuardDuty, cost_overview and the cover logo/background all consume it; missing assets fall back to the runtime Pillow renderer or are simply omitted.
- Page setup (_apply_page_setup): US Letter page_width=Inches(8.5)=12240 twips, page_height=Inches(11)=15840 twips. CHOSEN MARGINS (inches / EMU): left=0.25in (228600 EMU), right=0.3in (274320 EMU), top=0.9in (822960 EMU), bottom=0.8in (731520 EMU). Rendered pgMar (twips) = top=1296 right=432 bottom=1152 left=360 (close to reference top=1340 right=0 bottom=1160 left=360; right kept non-zero as a small printer gutter so the 6-col table is not clipped). Default body font Calibri 10pt (_apply_default_font).
- Cover (_build_cover): optional full-page cover_background via _add_full_page_background (inline picture converted to a wp:anchor behindDoc=1 drawing centered on the page - documented python-docx full-bleed limitation; absent by default so cover renders logo+bar+title only). Blue left accent bar via a 2-col borderless table col0 shaded _ACCENT_BLUE=1F4E79 (_shade_cell w:shd). Logo top-right (right-aligned run.add_picture width 1.8in). Large colored title + org + submitter + period. Ends with doc.add_page_break() so Cost Summary starts on page 2.
- Cost table (_build_cost_summary_differences): centered+underlined bold 16pt title paragraph. Stacked 'N'/'o' No header (run 'N' + run.add_break() + run 'o'). Two-line bold Last Week / Current Week headers (label + add_break() + '(<range>)' derived from _previous_range_str()/_current_range_str()). Service rows built first, then cols 0/1/2 vertically merged first_row.merge(last_row) -> emits w:vMerge (81 markers); merged cell shows '1' / account name / 674351849978, centered. Cost cells centered. Total Cost row: leading cells 0..3 merged into one centered bold 'Total Cost' cell (emits w:gridSpan); cost cols auto-labelled '(<total> Tax Excluded Cost)' with parentheses. Optional Cost Explorer overview image appended after the bullets.
- All new raw-OOXML helpers (_shade_cell, _center_cell, _two_line_bold_header, _stacked_no_header, _add_full_page_background, merges) wrapped in try/except -> log + continue. Python 3.9 compatible (typing.Optional/Union only, no 'X | None'; grep for '| None' etc. returns nothing).

VERIFIER (scripts/verify_word_report.py): extended with design_checks() that unzips word/document.xml and asserts: underlined+centered 'Cost Summary Differences' title; w:vMerge present; w:gridSpan on Total Cost; 'Last Week'/'Current Week' + w:br line breaks; pgSz Letter 12240x15840 + pgMar present; stacked N/o runs; word/media image count >= 6; cover logo drawing appears BEFORE the Cost Summary title. All existing content checks + CLI args (path, --contains, --min-images) kept.

FINAL VERIFIER OUTPUT: `python3 scripts/verify_word_report.py demo/Fly91_Weekly_Status_Report_14-20_Sep_2026.docx --min-images 7` -> 'ALL CHECKS PASSED  tables=8 paras=63 images=7' (exit 0). Images=7 = cover logo + 4 Inspector severity captures + GuardDuty + Cost Explorer overview (baseline was 5). FEAT-002 zipfile assertion: vMerge=81, pgSz present.

NO-REGRESSION: --format both -> wrote both .docx (256324 B) and Weekly_AWS_BAU_Report.xlsx (178336 B), exit 0. --format xlsx -> wrote .xlsx, exit 0. Excel path unaffected.

DATA-AGNOSTIC PROOF: ran scripts/verify_word_live_fallback.py (feeds a REAL-shaped payload with DIFFERENT account values, no cost.per_service, driving the service_breakdown fallback) -> 'ALL CHECKS PASSED (live data path)'. Then generated that live docx (--keep demo/live.docx) and ran the extended verifier against it: ALL 11 DESIGN assertions PASS (underline title, vMerge, gridSpan, two-line headers, pgSz Letter, stacked No, media>=6, cover logo before table). The 17 content-check failures on that run are expected - the minimal live fixture omits the mock-specific EC2/RDS IDs and the '400+' Inspector phrasing - but the DESIGN STRUCTURE is identical regardless of the mock flag, proving the layout is data-driven only in cell values. This mirrors how a real CloudShell run (no --mock) will look.

SANDBOX NOTE: /tmp does not persist between bash calls, so all generate+verify were chained in one invocation or written into demo/. Transient outputs (both.docx, x.xlsx, live.docx, Weekly_AWS_BAU_Report.xlsx, bau_report.log) were removed after verifying. Force-added (git add -f, since *.docx/*.png gitignored): demo/Fly91_Weekly_Status_Report_14-20_Sep_2026.docx + the 7 embedded assets (logo + 4 inspector + guardduty + cost_overview). cover_background.png intentionally NOT shipped (not in reference set) and the README documents the user must supply their own cityscape + swap the Operisoft/Aptech sample logo/captures for Greatworx/Fly91 via config.json word_report.assets. Reworked the helper to take (row, cell): it now emits w:trHeight on the row's w:trPr with w:val=13392 twips (~9.3in = 11in Letter page - 0.9in top - 0.8in bottom margins) and w:hRule='atLeast', so the shaded blue cell spans (close to) the full usable page height down the left edge. The anchor path is therefore now verified once with a real image; it remains guarded (only runs when the client supplies assets/cover_background.png) and the known full-bleed limitation is still documented in README.
